title: After-hours playing for the movie stars at Cafe Society
summary: Turner and Pete Johnson volunteered to stay after closing for famous patrons and made big tips.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I'd get out and sing...most o' the movie stars used to like to hear me sing "The Sheik of Araby," so I'd get out there and do my number and do my thing. So, in the evenin'...the nighttime when we closed up, they didn't wanna...all them movie stars didn't wanna go... go to the hotel, so they locked the door and stay in the nightclub. So, Barney Josephson ask who would like to stay to play after they got off, you know. Nobody wanted to do it. So me an' Pete Johnson say, "We'll stay."

So, then, we got to makin' so much money they got a wind o' it--the rest of them cats. We was down there, playin' an'...playin' an' singin' after hours, y'know. Was against the law but we was doin' it. And we was makin' hand over foot o' money. Tips. You know. They were tippin' us. So then ever'body else wanted to stay.
He say, "No. We got Joe and Pete Johnson. They started... they gonna stay."
So we stayed down there till four...five o'clock in the mornin' ...havin' a good time...makin' money.
